title: Tales of the Arabian Nights - a great time of random adventure
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LSGYVCqNEjc

Tales of the Arabian Nights (Z-Man edition) is one of the few games Daniel (@dungeondive) sold off at the end of one collecting phase and bought again at the start of the next. Returning to it after too long, he had a blast, and he suggests it's a fine training ground for solo roleplaying: the fun comes from stretching your imagination to connect wildly random events into a story.

His solo setup is two-handed, with house rules: race to 10 combined Destiny and Story points instead of 20, complete at least one quest, then return to Baghdad. He also splits a subset of the encounter deck into morning, noon and evening stacks so time of day actually turns over. Then he recounts the stories. Scheherazade, seeking love, is imprisoned by a wicked sage, finds love with her jailer, settles in Herat, has a child "as ugly as an elderly camel," catches wanderlust and wins. Ali Baba wakes from a shipwreck diseased and insane, is cured in León, learns the rumour of the Sepulchre of Solomon, fails to steal Solomon's ring, and washes up penniless.

He walks through the engine: encounter cards, the reaction matrices, the fate die nudging paragraph numbers, skills as gamebook keywords, and a huge list of statuses. His advice is to let go of strategy and enjoy the chaos. Over-think it and you'll have a bad time.

----

Have you ever had a run of Tales of the Arabian Nights so random it became a story you still retell? What happened?
